Symptoms: Comedones (blackheads and whiteheads), papules, pustules, cysts, and possible scarring
Prevalence: Approximately 50 million individuals in the USA are affected annually
Efficacy: Benzoyl peroxide is effective in reducing acne lesions by 5075% in many patients within 412 weeks of use
Safety: Generally considered safe for topical use; irritation can occur
Adverse_Events: Common adverse events include skin irritation, dryness, peeling, and redness; less common are allergic reactions or significant dermatitis
Age_Group: Commonly used in adolescents and young adults, typically ages 1225
Gender: Affects both genders, though prevalence may vary; more common in males during adolescence

Symptoms: Enlarged hands and feet, facial changes, joint pain, excessive sweating, headaches, vision problems, and other hormonal issues.
Prevalence: Approximately 36 cases per 1 million people in the USA; around 60,000 cases may exist in the U.S.
Efficacy: Generally effective in lowering growth hormone levels and reducing tumor size in patients with acromegaly.
Safety: Generally welltolerated, with regular monitoring recommended to avoid complications.
Adverse_Events: Potential side effects include injection site reactions, headaches, fatigue, and gastrointestinal issues.
Age_Group: Primarily adults aged 3050 years, but can occur at any age.
Gender: Affects both genders, with a slight male predominance.
Type_of_Drug: Longacting somatostatin analog (specific type of peptide therapy).

Symptoms: Difficulty breathing, swelling of the throat, hives, rapid pulse, low blood pressure, dizziness, gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting), confusion, loss of consciousness
Prevalence: Approximately 1.6% of the population experiences anaphylaxis at some point in their lives in the USA
Efficacy: Highly effective when administered promptly in treating anaphylactic reactions
Safety: Generally safe when used as directed; however, improper administration can lead to adverse outcomes
Adverse_Events: Possible adverse events include increased heart rate, hypertension, anxiety, and injection site reactions
Age_Group: All age groups can be affected, but specific kits are recommended for individuals at risk
Gender: Both genders are equally affected

Symptoms: Excessive worry, nervousness, restlessness, sleep disturbances, seizures
Prevalence: Approximately 19% of adults in the U.S. experience anxiety disorders at some time in their lives.
Efficacy: Lorazepam is effective for shortterm relief of anxiety symptoms, generally showing rapid onset of action.
Safety: Generally safe when used as prescribed; risk of dependence and withdrawal symptoms when used long term.
Adverse_Events: Sedation, dizziness, weakness, and in rare cases, paradoxical reactions (increased anxiety/agitation).
Age_Group: Typically prescribed for adults, but it can also be used cautiously in older adults.
Gender: Affects both genders; however, anxiety disorders may be more prevalent in females.

Symptoms: Redness, pain, swelling, blistering, and possibly peeling skin in the affected area.
Prevalence: Approximately 1.1 million cases of burn injuries occur annually in the USA, with varying severity.
Efficacy: Generally effective in providing pain relief and promoting healing of minor burns and skin irritations.
Safety: Considered safe when used as directed; however, caution is advised for individuals with known sensitivities.
Adverse_Events: Rare; potential skin irritation, allergies for some individuals.
Age_Group: Suitable for all age groups, with special considerations for very young children and elderly patients.
Gender: No specific gender preference; affects all genders equally.

Symptoms: Nasal congestion, facial pain/pressure, nasal discharge, reduced sense of smell, cough, fatigue
Prevalence: Approximately 12.1% of the adult population in the USA
Efficacy: Effective for symptom relief and clearance of nasal passages, especially in combination with other treatments.
Safety: Generally regarded as safe when used as directed.
Adverse_Events: Rare instances of nasal irritation, discomfort, or sinusitis exacerbation.
Age_Group: All ages; often more prevalent in adults.
Gender: Affects both genders, but may be more common in women.
Type_of_Drug: Nasal irrigation solution (not classified as a traditional drug; classified under physical therapies).

Symptoms: Cough, nasal congestion, sore throat, runny nose, sneezing, headache, mild fever
Prevalence: Approximately 1 billion colds occur annually in the USA, affecting adults and children alike.
Efficacy: Generally effective in providing symptomatic relief; however, it does not cure the cold.
Safety: Generally considered safe for shortterm use; consult with a physician for prolonged use.
Adverse_Events: Drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nausea, and gastrointestinal discomfort; side effects vary by individual.
Age_Group: Typically used in adults and children aged 12 and older; specific formulations may be available for younger children.
Gender: No significant gender differences in usage or efficacy.
Type_of_Drug: Combination overthecounter (OTC) cough and cold medication.

Symptoms: Redness, itching, burning sensations, rash, dry skin
Prevalence: Approximately 1520% of the U.S. population experiences contact dermatitis at some point in their lives.
Efficacy: Generally effective in cleansing affected areas and preventing further irritation.
Safety: Considered safe for topical use; however, additional factors such as individual skin sensitivity should be taken into account.
Adverse_Events: Possible local irritation, allergic reactions, and dryness.
Age_Group: All ages, although more common in adults due to occupational exposure.
Gender: Equal prevalence in both males and females, with slight variation depending on occupation and exposure risks.

Symptoms: Growth failure, renal tubular Fanconi syndrome, ocular symptoms (corneal deposits leading to photophobia and tearing), hypothyroidism, and muscle weakness.
Prevalence: Approximately 2,000 patients in the USA.
Efficacy: High efficacy in reducing cystine levels and preventing organ damage; effective in delaying renal failure.
Safety: Generally safe when monitored; main concern is adherence to dosing regimen to avoid toxicity.
Adverse_Events: Common adverse events include headache, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and potential renal impairment.
Age_Group: Primarily children and young adults; can be prescribed at any age after diagnosis.
Gender: Both males and females are affected equally.

Symptoms: Thirst, dry mouth, fatigue, dizziness, confusion, muscle cramps, low blood pressure
Prevalence: Common in various populations; specific prevalence rates depend on underlying conditions but dehydration can affect millions annually in the USA.
Efficacy: High efficacy in restoring fluid and electrolyte balance; widely used in clinical settings.
Safety: Generally welltolerated; low risk of serious side effects when used appropriately.
Adverse_Events: Possible rare adverse events include fluid overload, electrolyte imbalances, and vein irritation at the injection site.
Age_Group: Used across all age groups; particularly important for elderly and pediatric patients.
Gender: No significant gender predilection; applicable to all genders equally.

Symptoms: Redness, itching, inflammation, scaling, and thickened skin
Prevalence: Approximately 7.3% of the U.S. population is affected by eczema; psoriasis affects about 3.2%
Efficacy: Efficacy ranges around 7080% in clearing symptoms for moderate cases when used as directed
Safety: Generally considered safe for shortterm use; longterm use may lead to skin thinning and potential systemic absorption
Adverse_Events: Common adverse events include local irritation, burning sensation, and dryness; rare events may include systemic effects such as adrenal suppression
Age_Group: Approved for use in adults and children; typically prescribed for ages 2 years and older
Gender: No significant gender predisposition, affects all genders equally

Symptoms: Excessive thirst (polydipsia), increased urination (polyuria), dehydration.
Prevalence: Approximately 1 in 25,000 individuals (about 0.004%).
Efficacy: 8090% effective in managing symptoms in central diabetes insipidus.
Safety: Generally safe when used as prescribed; most patients tolerate it well.
Adverse_Events: Headache, nausea, abdominal cramps, nasal congestion (if using intranasal form).
Age_Group: All ages; commonly prescribed for both children and adults.
Gender: No significant gender preference; affects males and females equally.

Symptoms: Increased frequency of bowel movements, loose or watery stools, abdominal cramps, urgency to defecate.
Prevalence: Approximately 5% of the U.S. population experiences acute diarrhea annually.
Efficacy: Loperamide is highly effective for symptomatic relief of diarrhea, with studies showing an improvement in stool frequency in most patients.
Safety: Generally welltolerated; concerns exist with excessive use leading to serious complications.
Adverse_Events: Constipation, abdominal pain, dizziness, fatigue; rare cases of toxic megacolon.
Age_Group: Approved for use in adults and children over 6 years; not recommended for children under 6 years without medical supervision.
Gender: No significant gender differences in usage or efficacy.

Symptoms: Widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, sleep disturbances, cognitive difficulties, and tender points.
Prevalence: Approximately 2% of the adult population in the USA, predominantly affecting women.
Efficacy: Studies suggest SAVELLA (milnacipran) can reduce pain and improve function in approximately 30% to 50% of patients.
Safety: Generally well tolerated; common side effects include nausea, constipation, headache, dry mouth, and increased blood pressure.
Adverse_Events: Serious adverse events are rare but can include suicidal thoughts, seizures, and liver enzyme abnormalities.
Age_Group: Adults, typically ages 18 to 65.
Gender: Predominantly affects women, with a female to male ratio of approximately 7:1.
Type_of_Drug: Small molecule (specifically a serotoninnorepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, SNRI).

Symptoms: Developmental delays, intellectual disability, cardiovascular disease, skeletal abnormalities, eye disorders (such as lens dislocation), and thrombosis.
Prevalence: Approximately 1 in 200,000 to 1 in 300,000 individuals in the USA.
Efficacy: CYSTADANE (betaine anhydrous) is effective in lowering homocysteine levels in patients with homocystinuria, improving clinical outcomes.
Safety: Generally welltolerated; safety data indicate a low incidence of serious adverse effects when used as directed.
Adverse_Events: Common adverse events include nausea, abdominal discomfort, and diarrhea.
Age_Group: Primarily prescribed for children and adults with homocystinuria, typically diagnosed in infancy or early childhood.
Gender: No specific gender predisposition; affects both males and females equally.
Type_of_Drug: Small molecule (nutritional supplement that acts to lower homocysteine levels).

Symptoms: Severe hypertension (high blood pressure), headaches, visual disturbances, palpitations, shortness of breath, chest pain, and signs of heart failure.
Prevalence: Hypertensive crisis affects approximately 12% of the adult population in the USA annually.
Efficacy: Sodium nitroprusside is highly effective in rapidly lowering blood pressure, often within minutes, making it suitable for hypertensive emergencies.
Safety: Generally safe for acute use under medical supervision, but there are risks associated with prolonged infusion due to potential toxicity (cyanide toxicity).
Adverse_Events: Possible adverse events include hypotension (low blood pressure), headache, dizziness, reflex tachycardia, nausea, and, in rare cases, cyanide toxicity.
Age_Group: Primarily adults, although it can be used in pediatric populations under strict medical supervision.
Gender: Both genders are affected; however, hypertensive crises may be more prevalent in males due to higher rates of underlying risk factors.
Type_of_Drug: Small molecules (nitroprusside is a nitric oxide donor).

Symptoms: Weight loss, increased appetite, rapid heartbeat, anxiety, tremors, sweating, menstrual changes, and heat intolerance
Prevalence: Approximately 1.2% of the US population
Efficacy: High efficacy in diagnosing and managing hyperthyroidism and related conditions
Safety: Generally safe when used as directed for diagnostic imaging
Adverse_Events: Minor adverse events such as allergic reactions, transient hypothyroidism, or injection site reactions
Age_Group: Adolescents to older adults
Gender: More common in females, with a femaletomale ratio of about 5:1
Type_of_Drug: Radioactive iodine isotope (used in diagnostic imaging)

Symptoms: Swelling (edema), fatigue, weakness, increased susceptibility to infections, and potential for fluid accumulation in the lungs (pulmonary edema).
Prevalence: Approximately 45% of hospitalized patients.
Efficacy: Generally effective in raising serum albumin levels and improving clinical outcomes in patients who are hypoalbuminemic.
Safety: Generally welltolerated; special caution is recommended in patients with a history of allergic reactions to albumin products.
Adverse_Events: Potential for allergic reactions, fever, chills, headache, hypotension, and in rare cases, renal failure or thromboembolism.
Age_Group: Used in all age groups, but particularly in elderly patients and those with chronic conditions.
Gender: Both males and females are affected; no significant gender preference.

Symptoms: Muscle cramps, weakness, fatigue, irregular heart rhythms, nausea, vomiting, mental disturbances
Prevalence: Approximately 2% in the general population; higher in those with gastrointestinal diseases and certain chronic conditions
Efficacy: Generally effective in replenishing magnesium levels; specific efficacy varies based on underlying cause of deficiency
Safety: Welltolerated in most individuals; excessive amounts can lead to hypermagnesemia, especially in those with kidney impairment
Adverse_Events: Diarrhea, nausea, abdominal cramping, dizziness (more common with high doses)
Age_Group: All age groups; specific atrisk populations include older adults and those with chronic illnesses
Gender: No specific gender bias; effects are seen in all genders equally

Symptoms: Tingling or burning sensations in the fingers, muscle cramps, fatigue, and neck stiffness; severe cases may lead to seizures or cardiac issues.
Prevalence: Approximately 0.3 cases per 100,000 people in the USA; it is considered rare but can vary based on the population studied.
Efficacy: In clinical use, the efficacy of THYQUIDITY for managing symptom control in hypoparathyroidism is generally considered effective but varies among patients.
Safety: Welltolerated in the majority of patients; safety established through clinical trials and ongoing postmarket surveillance.
Adverse_Events: Common adverse events may include hypercalcemia, gastrointestinal upset, or hypersensitivity reactions.
Age_Group: Primarily adults, though it can occur in children.
Gender: More common in females than males, with a femaletomale ratio of approximately 3:1.
Type_of_Drug: Small molecule therapy (calcitriol and formulations aimed at managing calcium levels).

Symptoms: Muscle weakness, bone pain, fatigue, respiratory failure, increased susceptibility to infections
Prevalence: Approximately 12% of the general population, more common in patients with malnutrition or chronic illnesses
Efficacy: Effective in correcting electrolyte imbalances; efficacy is high in acute settings for phosphate replacement
Safety: Generally safe when used as directed; monitoring is necessary to prevent hyperphosphatemia
Adverse_Events: Possible adverse events include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and in rare cases, hypocalcemia or hyperphosphatemia
Age_Group: All age groups, most commonly used in adults
Gender: No significant gender predisposition; affects all genders equally

Symptoms: Bloating, diarrhea, gas, cramping, nausea, abdominal pain
Prevalence: Approximately 3050 million people in the USA (about 1520% of the population) experience lactose intolerance
Efficacy: High; lactase supplements significantly improve digestion of lactose in affected individuals
Safety: Generally considered safe with minimal side effects when used as directed
Adverse_Events: Rare; may include gastrointestinal discomfort in some individuals if taken in excessive amounts
Age_Group: All age groups; more common in adolescents and adults
Gender: Both genders are equally affected

Symptoms: Muscle rigidity, rapid heart rate, elevated body temperature, metabolic acidosis, increased carbon dioxide production, confusion or agitation.
Prevalence: Approximately 1 in 100,000 general anesthesia cases, prevalence of MH susceptibility in the general population is estimated at 1 in 15,000 to 1 in 50,000.
Efficacy: Dantrolene is effective in reversing the effects of malignant hyperthermia; studies indicate it can reduce mortality rates significantly when administered quickly.
Safety: Generally safe when used appropriately; however, requires cautious use in patients with liver disease.
Adverse_Events: Potential adverse events include drowsiness, dizziness, weakness, confusion, diarrhea, and risk of liver toxicity with chronic use.
Age_Group: Primarily used in adults; may be prescribed in adolescents and children based on medical need.
Gender: No specific gender predisposition; affects all genders equally.

Symptoms: Weight loss, muscle wasting, weakness, fatigue, impaired immune function
Prevalence: Approximately 12% of the general population, with higher rates in hospitalized patients (up to 40%)
Efficacy: Generally effective in improving nutritional status, with good outcomes in patients with severe malnutrition
Safety: Generally considered safe when used as directed; monitoring required for electrolytes and metabolic status
Adverse_Events: Possible complications include infections (from catheter use), metabolic imbalances (e.g., hyperglycemia), and liver dysfunction
Age_Group: All age groups, especially elderly and hospitalized individuals
Gender: No gender preference; used in both males and females

Symptoms: Cyanosis, fatigue, shortness of breath, dizziness, headache, increased heart rate
Prevalence: Approximately 1 in 50,000 to 1 in 100,000 live births in the USA
Efficacy: Methylene blue is generally effective, with response rates around 80% in acute cases
Safety: Generally considered safe when administered correctly; contraindicated in patients with G6PD deficiency
Adverse_Events: Headache, dizziness, urine discoloration (blue/green), gastrointestinal disturbances
Age_Group: All age groups; most commonly seen in infants
Gender: Both genders equally affected

Symptoms: Excessive daytime sleepiness, cataplexy, sleep paralysis, hallucinations, disrupted nighttime sleep
Prevalence: Approximately 0.02% to 0.05% of the population in the USA
Efficacy: Demonstrated to help reduce excessive daytime sleepiness in clinical trials  efficacy varies among individuals
Safety: Generally welltolerated; chronic usage may require monitoring for side effects
Adverse_Events: Commonly reported adverse events include insomnia, anxiety, headache, and discomfort at the injection site
Age_Group: Typically prescribed for adults and adolescents over the age of 7
Gender: Affects both genders equally, though studies show slightly higher prevalence in males

Symptoms: Stuffy or blocked nose, sinus pressure, runny nose, postnasal drip, sneezing
Prevalence: Approximately 20% of the US population experiences nasal congestion at least once per year
Efficacy: Generally effective for temporary relief of nasal congestion (7080% effective in reducing symptoms)
Safety: Considered safe for shortterm use; longterm safety data is limited due to potential for misuse
Adverse_Events: Commonly reported events include insomnia, nervousness, restlessness, and increased heart rate; serious adverse events are rare
Age_Group: Commonly used in all age groups, but specific caution is advised for children under 12 and individuals over 65
Gender: Equally effective in both genders

Symptoms: Respiratory depression, loss of consciousness, pinpoint pupils, decreased heart rate, and potentially death
Prevalence: In 2021, approximately 100,000 fatal overdoses occurred in the USA, with opioid overdoses being a significant portion of this number; opioid misuse affects millions, with estimates indicating around 2 million individuals having an opioid use disorder.
Efficacy: Naloxone is highly effective in reversing opioid overdose when administered timely; studies show effective reversal in over 90% of cases with proper administration.
Safety: Generally regarded as safe; naloxone has a favorable safety profile, with minimal side effects in cases of accidental administration in nonopioid users.
Adverse_Events: Symptoms may include opioid withdrawal in dependent individuals, such as agitation, nausea, vomiting, and rapid heart rate; however, serious adverse events are rare.
Age_Group: All age groups, particularly among individuals at high risk for opioid overdose, including young adults and older adults.
Gender: Affects all genders, with some studies indicating higher rates of opioid use disorder in males compared to females, but overdose rates have increased in both sexes.

Symptoms: Abdominal pain, bloating, indigestion, nausea, loss of appetite, weight loss.
Prevalence: Approximately 4.5 million adults in the USA experience peptic ulcers at some point in their lives.
Efficacy: Sucralfate is effective in healing ulcers with a healing rate of about 7090% over a treatment course of 48 weeks.
Safety: Generally considered safe for shortterm use, with minimal systemic absorption.
Adverse_Events: Common adverse events include constipation (up to 2%) and minor gastrointestinal discomfort. Rarely, hypersensitivity reactions may occur.
Age_Group: Primarily affects adults, typically age 30 and older.
Gender: More common in men, but women are also significantly affected; overall incidence is increasing in postmenopausal women.
Type_of_Drug: Small molecule drug, specifically a gastroprotective agent.

Symptoms: Intellectual disability, behavioral problems, seizures, skin rashes, and musty odor in breath or urine due to accumulation of phenylalanine
Prevalence: Approximately 1 in 10,000 to 15,000 newborns in the USA
Efficacy: Improved blood phenylalanine levels in about 6080% of treated individuals
Safety: Generally considered safe; main concerns are dietary adherence and potential for phenylalanine increases
Adverse_Events: Mild headaches, gastrointestinal disturbances, and allergic reactions
Age_Group: All ages, particularly newborns for initial screening and treatment
Gender: No significant gender predilection; affected equally

Symptoms: Fatigue, jaundice, anemia, pale skin, shortness of breath, rapid heart rate, dark urine, enlarged spleen
Prevalence: Approximately 1 in 100,000 individuals in the USA; more common in specific ethnic groups (e.g., people of Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and African descent)
Efficacy: Clinical trials demonstrate a significant increase in hemoglobin levels and a reduction in transfusion requirements for patients with pyruvate kinase deficiency
Safety: Generally welltolerated; longterm safety data is still being compiled as it is a newer therapy
Adverse_Events: Most common adverse events include headache, diarrhea, nausea, and fatigue
Age_Group: Primarily adults, but can also be diagnosed in children; ages 1865 years commonly affected
Gender: Affects both males and females equally
Type_of_Drug: Small molecule (PYRUKYND is specifically a PK activator)

Symptoms: Fever, headache, confusion, agitation, paralysis, hydrophobia, hallucinations, seizures, and eventually coma or death.
Prevalence: Rabies is reported in about 1 to 3 cases annually in the USA, with higher incidence in certain animals.
Efficacy: Highly effective when administered postexposure before symptoms develop.
Safety: Generally safe when used appropriately; however, allergic reactions can occur.
Adverse_Events: Localized pain at the injection site, fever, headache, allergic reactions.
Age_Group: All age groups (most common in children due to higher exposure risks).
Gender: No significant gender predilection.

Symptoms: Fatigue, swollen and bleeding gums, joint pain, anemia, skin issues (including rash and bruising), and poor wound healing.
Prevalence: Approximately 0.1% of the U.S. population is estimated to be affected by scurvy, with higher prevalence in certain groups, such as those with limited access to fresh fruits and vegetables.
Efficacy: High efficacy in alleviating symptoms of scurvy, with improvement typically seen within days of administration.
Safety: Generally safe with low risk of toxicity; excess in very high doses may cause gastrointestinal disturbances.
Adverse_Events: Rare; potential for diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal cramps in sensitive individuals.
Age_Group: All age groups, but especially observed in adults and the elderly who may not have adequate diets.
Gender: Both genders are equally affected by vitamin C deficiency.

Symptoms: Low blood pressure, rapid heart rate, confusion, fever, shortness of breath, decreased urine output
Prevalence: Approximately 13 cases per 1,000 hospital admissions in the USA
Efficacy: GIAPREZA has been shown to improve blood pressure in patients with septic or neurogenic shock, with certain studies indicating a significant increase in mean arterial pressure
Safety: Generally considered safe; however, blood pressure should be closely monitored during administration
Adverse_Events: Hypotension, elevated blood pressure, tachycardia, and arrhythmias are noted adverse events
Age_Group: Primarily adults, but can be used in pediatric populations with careful monitoring
Gender: No gender preference; affects both males and females equally

Symptoms: Prolonged seizures, confusion, loss of consciousness, muscle spasms
Prevalence: Approximately 150,000 cases of status epilepticus occur in the USA annually
Efficacy: NAYZILAM has shown efficacy in terminating seizure episodes with rapid onset of action
Safety: Generally considered safe for use, with a favorable safety profile in acute settings
Adverse_Events: Common adverse events include sedation, somnolence, dizziness, and potential respiratory depression
Age_Group: Approved for use in adults and children aged 12 years and older
Gender: No specific genderbased restrictions; used in both males and females
Type_of_Drug: Nasal spray formulation of the small molecule drug midazolam

Symptoms: Redness, pain, swelling, blistering, peeling skin, heat sensation.
Prevalence: Approximately 35% of adults in the USA report experiencing sunburn each year.
Efficacy: Generally effective for symptomatic relief of pain, redness, and inflammation associated with sunburn.
Safety: Generally safe when used as directed; low risk of systemic side effects.
Adverse_Events: Localized irritation, allergic reactions, and skin sensitivity in some users.
Age_Group: All age groups (typically used by adults and children).
Gender: Both genders equally affected; usage may vary based on sun exposure habits.
Type_of_Drug: Topical analgesic and antiinflammatory gel (not a prescription drug).

Symptoms: Sores, rashes, fever, fatigue, swollen lymph nodes, pain, and affected organ systems depending on the infection
Prevalence: Approximately 0.1% for syphilis (as of 2021)
Efficacy: Highly effective, with cure rates exceeding 95% for early syphilis
Safety: Generally safe when used as directed; however, caution in patients with penicillin allergies
Adverse_Events: Allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis (rare), rash, fever, urticaria
Age_Group: All age groups, but higher prevalence in sexually active adults
Gender: More common in men, particularly men who have sex with men

Symptoms: Eye redness, blurred vision, light sensitivity, floaters, pain in the eye
Prevalence: Approximately 38,000 cases of uveitis are reported annually in the USA
Efficacy: Clinical studies show that YUTIQ provides sustained reduction in inflammation with improved visual outcomes in 7080% of patients
Safety: Generally welltolerated; ongoing monitoring is necessary due to potential side effects
Adverse_Events: Increased intraocular pressure (IOP), cataract formation, eye pain, and retinal detachment
Age_Group: Primarily adults aged 1865 years
Gender: Affects both males and females equally, though incidence can vary based on underlying autoimmune conditions
